ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Under Articles 3, 4, 10 and 11 of Ley 10/2010 and Real Decreto 304/2014, the incorporating corporate service provider and notary must (i) identify every direct shareholder holding 25% or more of capital or voting rights and every indirect ultimate beneficial owner exercising control; (ii) classify Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) of all relevant jurisdictions per FATF methodology; and (iii) screen all parties against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists (for USD wire and SWIFT LC clearing relevance), and the Spanish domestic sanctions and counter-terrorism designations maintained by the Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores. Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced banking tier applicable to ISIC 4659 used heavy machinery remarketing, enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory and requires documentary source-of-funds evidence, counterparty trade-risk scoring, negative-news monitoring, and prior clearance before execution of any Swift LC or wire transfer. All personal data handling must comply with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and Ley Orgánica 3/2018.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) online denomination service operated by the Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad, Mercantiles y de Bienes Muebles de España and accessible through the Sede Electrónica of the Ministerio de Justicia (https://www.mjusticia.gob.es/sede)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Governing rules: Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1784/1996), Articles 378-407. The company denomination must be expressed in Spanish or in any official language of the Spanish State (Catalan/Valencian, Galician, Basque), written exclusively in Roman characters, and must contain the legal form ending 'S.L.' or the full phrase 'Sociedad Limitada' (or 'S.L.U.' where the sole-shareholder form is intended). Spanish orthography (ñ, accents, diacritics) is permitted; any foreign-language or non-Latin-script commercial token must be rendered in a Spanish-readable transliteration accepted by the Registry. The denomination must be orthographically and phonetically distinctive from all existing registered names; purely generic or descriptive tokens that do not achieve sufficient specificity are refused.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Toponyms of Spanish autonomous communities and provinces (e.g., Andalucía, Cataluña, País Vasco, Galicia) when used as exclusive identifiers
Expressions contrary to law, public order, or good morals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative denomination certificate is valid for three months from issuance, within which the public deed of incorporation must be executed (Article 418, Reglamento del Registro Mercantil). There is no automatic extension; upon expiry, a fresh application may be submitted for the same or alternative names. If the Registro Mercantil Central rejects the proposed denomination (identity, confusing similarity, or prohibited token), the incorporator shall within fifteen working days of notification submit a corrected online application containing up to five alternative denominations in descending order of preference, and the Central Registry will certify the first available and lawful option. If rejection persists, an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) lies to the Dirección General de la Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministerio de Justicia within fifteen working days under Ley 39/2015, Articles 121-122, which must resolve within three months; a further judicial remedy before the Juzgado de lo Contencioso-Administrativo (Ley 29/1998) is available against the administrative decision. In market practice, re-filing with a modified distinctive token is the fastest remedy and typically yields certification within two to three working days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only as a transitional substance arrangement provided the serviced or virtual office is a physically located Spanish address managed under an executed lease or service agreement, and the company's books, records, and management facilities can be produced at that address. A pure postal box or accommodation address does not satisfy the real-seat doctrine of Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010) and will be treated by the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and SEPBLAC as a sham-seat indicator. For the licensed-free used-machinery wholesale activity, a serviced business-hub office (Madrid, Barcelona, or Valencia) is market-acceptable at inception, but the company should migrate to a leased warehouse or commercial office within the first operating year; corporate banks applying enhanced due diligence for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier normally require proof of a full lease or executive serviced-office agreement before onboarding.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 12% annualized probability of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first three operating years for a medium-risk wholesale trading SL, rising to an estimated 30% where the registered office is a virtual address or the company files zero or predominantly foreign-sourced turnover. Inspections originate principally from AEAT VAT and invoice verification audits and from SEPBLAC's cyclical AML/CFT inspection plan covering non-financial obliged entities; an on-site verification is highly probable where annual turnover exceeds EUR 1,000,000 or a single intra-EU transaction exceeds EUR 50,000.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, particularly Articles 19-23, 28-30, 32-35, 58-63, 210-242, and 285-290. The Electronic and Digital Corporate Law reforms, including Law 18/2022, also apply to simplified and electronic formation procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent authority is the Registro Mercantil of the province where the registered office is located. Name availability is obtained from the Registro Mercantil Central.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), followed by an application for registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be incorporated with minimum share capital of EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation; no statutory escrow account is required. Until the company reaches EUR 3,000 of capital plus legal reserves, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to the legal reserve until the combined amount reaches EUR 3,000. In liquidation, shareholders may be jointly liable for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the company's subscribed capital if the company cannot satisfy its liabilities. Notary and Mercantile Registry charges are separate regulated professional fees and are not included in the stated state filing fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and records the subscription and full payment of its issued share capital by the founding shareholder in accordance with the deed of incorporation; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted and entered in the Company's records; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, where applicable, the directors named in the deed are confirmed, each with the powers stated in the articles and applicable law; (4) the officers are authorised to obtain tax, municipal, banking, customs, and operational registrations and to execute all filings required to commence the Company's wholesale machinery activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreigner Identification and Corporate Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria), Police immigration authorities where applicable, and Registro Mercantil Central online name-clearance service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain an NIE for each non-resident shareholder, director, and authorised representative requiring one. Request a negative certificate of company name from the Registro Mercantil Central, listing alternative names in priority order. Reserve the approved name within its validity period and use the exact approved wording in all formation documents.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity document of each shareholder and director
NIE certificates or applications, where required
Power of attorney, if filings are handled by a representative
Foreign corporate shareholder documents, if applicable, apostilled or legalised and translated by a sworn Spanish translator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name. If an NIE or identity file is queried, provide the missing identification, representation, apostille, or sworn translation through the competent authority or authorised representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles, Shareholding, and Beneficial Ownership Package
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected Spanish notary public and, where electronic incorporation is used, the Centralised Notarial Information and Processing System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association, business purpose, registered office, capital and quota allocation, management structure, director identification, shareholder details, beneficial ownership statement, and corporate powers. Confirm that the business purpose accurately covers wholesale trading, import, export, storage, repair coordination, and remarketing of used construction machinery, without implying regulated waste treatment or manufacturing unless separately authorised.
required_dossiers: Registered-office title, lease, or owner authorisation
Foreign shareholder constitutional documents and incumbency evidence
Power of attorney for signing representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent names, addresses, ownership percentages, purpose clauses, or powers of attorney. Re-execute or notarise deficient documents before the deed is signed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed and Pay Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the escritura pública de constitución. State the capital subscribed by each shareholder and evidence full payment. A bank certificate may be used for cash contributions, although a certificate is generally not required where the founders accept statutory responsibility for the reality of the contribution. Non-cash contributions require a detailed description, valuation, ownership evidence, and transfer documentation.
required_dossiers: Contribution and ownership evidence for non-cash assets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary must identify and cure formal deficiencies before execution. If the notary refuses authorisation, request the legal basis, correct the defect, and resubmit or seek review through the applicable notarial procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and File Corporate Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria), using Form 036 and the applicable electronic filing channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the provisional Spanish tax identification number, register the company census details, identify directors and beneficial owners where required, select the appropriate economic activities, and state VAT and intra-Community transaction status where applicable. After Mercantile Registry registration, file the amendment or confirmation to obtain the definitive tax identification number.
required_dossiers: Notarised incorporation deed or certified copy
Electronic certificate or authorised representative credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond electronically or through the appointed representative to any requerimiento, correcting census codes, identity data, tax residence evidence, or representation documents. Submit the definitive tax identification update after registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial for the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarised incorporation deed electronically through the notary or directly through the authorised filing channel. Pay the applicable Mercantile Registry tariff, monitor the registry entry, and obtain the registration certificate or registry extract. Confirm that the registered office, directors, capital, ownership quotas, business purpose, and beneficial ownership information are correctly recorded.
required_dossiers: Registry application and authorised filing details
Payment evidence for applicable registry charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a qualification notice, correct the stated defect within the statutory validity period, provide supplementary documents, or appeal the qualification under the Spanish Mercantile Registry review and appeal procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Incorporation Corporate and Commercial Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency, relevant autonomous-community authorities, municipal authority, Customs and Excise authorities, and Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legalise mandatory accounting books electronically through the Mercantile Registry, obtain the definitive tax identification number, register intra-Community transactions and EORI where required, register for municipal economic activity and premises procedures, and assess warehouse, opening, signage, fire, occupational safety, environmental, and transport obligations before operations begin.
required_dossiers: Registered incorporation deed and registry extract
EORI application, if importing or exporting
Environmental or waste-management documentation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer municipal, tax, customs, or regional authority queries with corrected forms and technical documents. Do not commence an activity requiring prior authorisation until the authorisation, declaration, or responsible statement has become legally effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent authority is generally the industry department of the autonomous community where the premises are located, together with the relevant municipal authority. The Ministry of Industry and Tourism is the national coordinating authority but normally does not issue a general wholesale machinery trading licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general national manufacturing or industrial operating licence is normally required for wholesale remarketing of used hydraulic excavators and rollers. A municipal activity licence, prior communication, or responsible declaration for the warehouse or commercial premises may be required under the applicable autonomous-community and municipal rules.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental authority of the relevant autonomous community, applying Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment and applicable regional legislation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from full project-level EIA for ordinary wholesale storage and trading without manufacturing, waste treatment, significant fuel storage, or material environmental transformation. Municipal environmental screening or an environmental activity authorisation may nevertheless be required. If the company receives machinery classified as waste or performs dismantling, depollution, recycling, or waste treatment, separate waste-management authorisation under Law 7/2022 and regional rules may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single Spain-wide wholesale-trading threshold applies. Any wastewater discharge must comply with the municipal sewer ordinance or a discharge permit and applicable industrial wastewater limits. Storage and handling must prevent oil, hydraulic-fluid, fuel, and contaminated-soil releases; spills and hazardous waste must be managed through authorised waste operators under Law 7/2022. VOC, dust, noise, and air-emission limits apply only where the premises or equipment generate regulated emissions under national, regional, or municipal rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before opening, obtain or file the municipal activity, opening, or responsible declaration required for the premises and demonstrate compliance with the Spanish Building Code, fire-safety rules under Royal Decree 513/2017, and applicable municipal fire requirements. Maintain emergency routes, extinguishers, fire detection and compartmentation where required, and obtain technical certificates or inspections for structural load and machinery areas. Comply with occupational risk-prevention duties under Law 31/1995, including risk assessment, worker training, personal protective equipment, lifting and traffic controls, and coordination with contractors. A separate industrial safety registration may apply if regulated installations, pressure equipment, fuel storage, or electrical installations are installed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — official portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) first obtains a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) upon execution of the public incorporation deed before a notary; the definitive corporate NIF is then issued via Form 036/037 filed with the AEAT before commencement of activity. The SL, as a tax-resident company, is registered in the Censo de Obligados Tributarios under its corporate NIF. Non-resident foreign shareholders do not require a separate Spanish tax ID for the SL's incorporation; however, any foreign parent or related entity engaging in Spanish taxable transactions must obtain a NIF (letter 'N' regime) through Form 036 and, where required, appoint a tax representative resident in Spain. The SL's definitive NIF is thereafter used for all VAT, Corporate Income Tax, customs, and statistical reporting obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades at the standard 25% rate on worldwide income as a tax resident; non-resident shareholders are taxed separately under the Non-Resident Income Tax regime, while the entity itself is not eligible for pass-through treatment under Spanish law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a check-the-box or equivalent elective classification regime. Statutory elections available include the tax consolidation regime (grupo de consolidación fiscal) under Articles 61-80 of Ley 27/2014 (LIS), requiring 75% direct or indirect ownership and minimum 6-month shareholding; optional free-depreciation and accelerated-depreciation rules; R&D and technological innovation tax-credit elections; the participation-exemption election for qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains; and the tonnage-tax regime for qualifying shipping groups. Hybrid-mismatch corrective rules under ATAD/DAC are mandatorily applied via LIS Articles 15 bis and 18 bis, with no elective opt-out.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.scope_note: The SL's stated non-resident ownership is fully permitted under Spanish law; minimum capital of EUR 1 is formally permitted but, in practice, the standard statutory minimum of EUR 3,000 is typically observed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.note: Resident SLs are treated as separate taxable persons for VAT and corporate income tax; no single-member disregarded-entity election exists for a Spanish SL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic-turnover threshold for VAT registration: registration is mandatory before the first taxable supply under Ley 37/1992 (LIVA). The simplified-regime (régimen simplificado) is available only for qualifying small businesses with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 250,000; retailers may use the equivalence-surcharge regime (recargo de equivalencia) up to EUR 150,000 annual turnover. For the wholesale remarketing of used construction excavators, the principal registration obligation is the ordinary censal declaration via Form 036 prior to any transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing is introduced by Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), phased in from 2024-2025, requiring interoperable e-invoice formats. Large taxpayers with turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000 and VAT groups must submit all invoice records to AEAT in near real time under the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system within 4 calendar days of issuance; the Verifactu Regulation (Real Decreto 1007/2023) requires the use of AEAT-compliant billing software with QR-code and hash-chain features by all applicable taxpayers from 2025. Customs export declarations are filed electronically via the DUES (Declaración Única Administrativa) / Sumisi贸n EDI system operated by the Agencia Tributaria's Customs Department.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of used hydraulic earthmovers and rollers to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT with full deduction of input VAT under LIVA Article 21, provided the goods physically leave EU territory within 3 months of dispatch and the exporter retains adequate proof of export. Intra-Community supplies to a VAT-registered customer in another Member State are exempt under LIVA Article 25 if the customer's valid VIES identification number is obtained and the goods are transported out of Spain to another Member State. Export transactions are zero-rated irrespective of the used-goods margin scheme under Article 128 LIVA; however, the exporter must obtain the export evidence within the applicable legal deadline and include the supplies in the periodic VAT return and recapitulative statement (Form 349) where applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Documento Único Administrativo / DUA) with MRN number
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR international consignment note evidencing physical departure from Spain/EU territory
Commercial invoice, pro-forma invoice, and, if used, sales contract or purchase order for the used machinery
Packing list with machine identification and serial numbers matching the DUA
Proof of delivery at destination signed by the non-EU customer or carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103 credit advice, or bank statement evidencing receipt of export payment
Intrastat dispatch declaration if goods move to another EU Member State
Documentation of the supplier's VAT registration and VIES validation where an intra-Community supply exemption is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may retrospectively claw back all input VAT deducted on zero-rated exports if the export is not fully documented within the statutory records, adding late-payment interest under Article 191 LGT. Infringements under LIVA Article 170 attract fixed penalties of EUR 300 to EUR 6,000 per invoice per unit, or proportional penalties of 50%-150% of the undeclared tax; knowingly fraudulent export zero-rating or false export documentation constitutes criminal tax fraud under Article 305 and 305 bis of the Spanish Criminal Code where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 6 years, fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, and loss of tax benefits or public subsidies. Customs declaration errors additionally trigger sanctions under Real Decreto 328/2018 (Reglamento General de Actuaciones y Procedimientos de Gestión e Inspección Tributaria), and refund claims may be refused or suspended where the exporter fails to provide coherent and verifiable export evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, acting within the Eurosystem under the authority of the European Central Bank. Foreign-investment reporting is principally administered by the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise under Spain's foreign-investment regulations. Spain applies the EU framework for payment services, capital movements, sanctions, anti-money laundering, and financial-market conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and has a fully liberalized current-account and capital-account regime subject to EU and Spanish anti-money-laundering, sanctions, tax, prudential, and statistical-reporting rules. A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may generally receive foreign capital, convert funds, pay suppliers, distribute dividends, repay qualifying shareholder loans, and remit profits without prior foreign-exchange approval. Banks may require evidence of the commercial purpose, beneficial ownership, source of funds, underlying contracts, tax compliance, and sanctions screening. Dividend distributions require distributable profits, approval under Spanish corporate law, maintenance of legally required reserves, and documentation of applicable Spanish withholding tax or treaty relief. Interest, royalties, management fees, and related-party payments require arm's-length support, transfer-pricing documentation, withholding-tax analysis, and beneficial-owner evidence. Non-resident foreign investments, acquisitions, disposals, and certain changes in ownership may trigger declarations to the Ministry of Economy, including filings under Royal Decree 571/2023 and its implementing rules. Certain foreign investments in strategic sectors, or investments involving regulated or security-sensitive activities, may require prior authorization; ordinary wholesale trading of used excavators and rollers is not ordinarily a strategic-sector activity, but the facts should be screened before closing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a Spanish bank, convert a mandatory percentage of export receipts into euros, or complete conversion within a prescribed export-receipt deadline. Export proceeds may generally be retained in foreign currency or received into an eligible euro or foreign-currency account, subject to banking, tax, customs, sanctions, and accounting controls. The company must retain commercial invoices, customs or transport evidence where applicable, purchase orders, bills of lading, delivery evidence, and payment records. Cross-border payment and external-position information may be reportable through Banco de España statistical reporting systems, particularly for entities meeting applicable reporting thresholds or receiving specific reporting requests. Export VAT treatment, customs declarations, Intrastat obligations where applicable, and tax records remain separate from foreign-exchange rules. Cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more when entering or leaving the EU, and certain domestic cash movements of EUR 100,000 or more, are subject to Spanish declaration requirements; banks may also impose transaction-level monitoring and documentary requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account for incorporation or capital increase, followed by a Spanish resident operational current account and foreign-currency account where available
Capital deposit account for incorporation or capital increase, followed by a Spanish resident operational current account and trade-finance account
Capital deposit account for incorporation or capital increase, followed by an operational current account, payment account, and documentary-trade facility
Capital deposit account for incorporation or capital increase, followed by an operational current account and import-export trade-finance account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. An EU-authorized electronic money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, SEPA transfers, foreign-exchange services, and international payment execution through passporting or an authorized Spanish branch or agent, subject to its license perimeter and local registration status. An electronic money account is not a bank deposit and does not provide the same deposit-guarantee protection as a credit institution; customer funds must be safeguarded under the applicable payment-services rules. An offshore non-EU EMI generally cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to Spanish customers solely through an offshore website without an appropriate EU authorization, passport, branch, agent, or other legally valid access route. Fintechs may reject used-heavy-machinery trading because of sanctions exposure, high-value goods, complex logistics, third-country counterparties, unusual payment corridors, cash intensity, or insufficient transaction history. The Spanish SL should retain at least one fully regulated Spanish or EEA credit-institution relationship for payroll, taxes, customs, trade finance, and contingency liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available where the institution can complete legally compliant customer identification, qualified or acceptable electronic identification, beneficial-owner verification, powers-of-attorney validation, video identification where used, source-of-funds review, and sanctions screening. Individual bank policy frequently requires a director, authorized signatory, or beneficial owner to attend an in-person or video interview, especially for a newly incorporated SL, non-resident owners, complex ownership chains, high-risk jurisdictions, foreign-currency activity, or trade-finance facilities. A Spanish resident registered office, Spanish tax identification number, commercial-register evidence, verified business activity, and a coherent first-year transaction forecast materially improve remote-onboarding viability. The bank may require notarized, apostilled, legalized, or sworn-translated documents depending on the issuing jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner with an opaque ownership chain, nominee arrangement, trust, bearer-share history, or inconsistent ownership information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current commercial-register extracts for every intermediate entity; certified constitutional documents; complete ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; beneficial-owner declaration; board and shareholder resolutions; notarized or apostilled powers of attorney; explanation of control rights; and a written confirmation that no nominee, bearer-share, or undisclosed controlling arrangement exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign capital injection with unexplained source of funds, round-sum transfers, third-party remitters, or payment from an account not held by the shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription or capital-increase resolution; bank transfer confirmation from the shareholder's account; shareholder bank statements; audited financial statements; tax returns or sale agreements supporting wealth origin; loan agreement where funding is debt; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth memorandum; beneficial-owner evidence; and reconciliation between the incoming amount, accounting entry, and corporate-register filing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Used construction machinery activity involving high-value assets, cash purchases, unusual price discounts, rapid resale, multiple intermediaries, or counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; inventory and asset-identification procedure; serial-number and ownership checks; invoices; purchase and resale contracts; valuation methodology; transport and delivery records; customs documents; sanctions and restricted-party screening policy; anti-bribery policy; payment policy prohibiting unexplained third-party payments and excessive cash; customer and supplier due-diligence files; and sample transaction-flow map.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment corridors involving sanctioned countries, sanctioned persons, embargo-sensitive goods, military end users, or potentially dual-use machinery
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC; end-user and end-use certificates; export-control classification; EU and UN sanctions screening records; transport-route analysis; customs classification; licensing or non-licensing determination; contractual sanctions clauses; independent compliance review; and documented escalation and rejection procedures. No transaction should proceed where applicable sanctions or export-control authorization is absent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared business activity, expected turnover, account geography, payment currencies, and actual transaction behavior
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy; twelve-month cash-flow forecast; country and currency matrix; expected monthly transaction volumes; supplier and customer list; representative contracts and invoices; warehouse or logistics agreements; VAT and tax-registration evidence; payroll and operating-cost budget; and quarterly account-monitoring review signed by management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on offshore digital EMIs, virtual IBANs, payment intermediaries, or nested accounts for core operating activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider authorization and passporting evidence; account-holder and safeguarding disclosures; contractual terms; explanation of each payment intermediary; transaction-flow chart; reconciliation controls; proof that the account is in the company's legal name; contingency banking plan; and confirmation that regulated banking, tax, customs, payroll, and trade-finance obligations will not be bypassed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner, director, authorized signatory, or major counterparty identified as a politically exposed person or associated person
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP disclosure; role and appointment history; enhanced source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; independent adverse-media search; government salary, asset, tax, or business-interest evidence where appropriate; risk-based approval by senior management; enhanced transaction monitoring; and documented absence of bribery, corruption, or public-procurement conflicts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete Spanish corporate records, missing tax identification number, inconsistent registered address, or inability to verify operating substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of incorporation; current Registro Mercantil extract; Spanish tax identification certificate; registered office evidence; lease, warehouse, or logistics agreement; director and signatory appointments; shareholder register or ownership statement; municipal or sector registration where relevant; invoices and contracts; and evidence of actual management and operational decision-making.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a regulated Spanish or EEA credit institution into the SL's corporate account, with the remitter named exactly as the subscribing shareholder or documented lender. Use a clear transfer narrative such as 'capital contribution', 'share subscription', 'capital increase', or 'shareholder loan', supported by the relevant shareholder and board resolutions. For SWIFT payments, provide accurate ordering-customer, beneficiary, ultimate-beneficiary, and purpose information; do not use personal accounts, undisclosed third parties, cash, or payment agents. For an incorporation or capital increase, obtain the bank's capital-deposit certificate where required by the notary and corporate-registration process, then transfer funds to the operational account after registration. Reconcile the bank credit to the accounting ledger and corporate filing. Review foreign-investment declaration requirements under Royal Decree 571/2023 and applicable Ministry of Economy forms, including any threshold, sector, ownership-change, or periodic reporting obligation. Retain bank advices, resolutions, subscription documents, loan agreements, source-of-funds evidence, tax records, and foreign-exchange reporting evidence. SEPA transfers are appropriate for euro-denominated EEA payments; SWIFT is appropriate for non-SEPA or multi-currency payments. Banks may request a payment purpose, supporting documents, and beneficial-owner verification even though Spain has no general capital-control approval process.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area, subject to bank limits and fraud controls. Use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly evidenced by an MT103 or its ISO 20022 successor message, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency supplier payments; include complete originator, beneficiary, bank, invoice, goods description, and purpose information. For substantial machinery imports, use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit, preferably subject to UCP 600, with presentation conditions covering commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, insurance where required, inspection certificate, serial numbers, origin evidence, and sanctions or end-user representations. Consider documentary collection under URC 522 for lower-risk counterparties, and open-account terms only after credit and sanctions due diligence. Match each payment to a purchase order, invoice, contract, customs or transport record, and goods-receipt evidence. Verify beneficiary bank-account changes through an independent channel. Avoid third-party payments unless approved, documented, and accepted by the bank. Apply VAT, customs, withholding-tax, transfer-pricing, and import-control analysis separately from the payment-clearing decision. Maintain segregation of duties for payment initiation, approval, sanctions screening, and bank reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an authorized bank or investment firm to hedge documented forecast or committed EUR, USD, GBP, or other foreign-currency machinery purchases and sales. The notional, tenor, currency, and maturity should be proportionate to identifiable commercial exposure.
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity and currency-management purposes, subject to counterparty credit limits, documented commercial exposure, collateral terms, and treasury approval.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency is non-convertible or market convention requires cash settlement. NDFs do not create a route around Spanish, EU, sanctions, tax, or capital-movement rules and should be entered only with an appropriately authorized counterparty.

Currency options and collars may be used for documented trade exposures where the company understands premium, settlement, break-cost, and potential-obligation risks. The company should avoid speculative or leveraged structures unrelated to its operating exposure.

Cross-currency swaps may be appropriate for material, longer-term shareholder or bank financing, subject to counterparty documentation, valuation, collateral, accounting, and interest-rate risk controls.

Hedging documentation should specify the exposure, hedge ratio, authorized counterparties, ISDA or equivalent master documentation, confirmations, collateral and margin obligations, valuation controls, accounting treatment under applicable Spanish GAAP or IFRS, EMIR-related reporting and risk-mitigation requirements where applicable, and periodic effectiveness review. Derivatives involving an EU investment firm or bank remain subject to MiFID II, EMIR, market-conduct, suitability or appropriateness, reporting, and prudential requirements as applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Cuentas Anuales (Annual Accounts Deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) and Registro Mercantil Central
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit triggers fines up to €6,000, 'cierre registral' (suspension of all registry filings for the company), and loss of certain corporate incentives; repeated non-deposit may lead to formal strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days from the close of the six-month period following fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing accrues surcharges of 10% to 20% of the outstanding tax liability plus late-payment interest; non-filing penalties may reach 20% of the amount due, with additional fines for inaccurate or incomplete declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No standalone fixed annual deadline; reported within 30 days of any beneficial-owner change, and verified during the annual accounts deposit process
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or communicate UBO information may result in fines under AML Law 10/2010 of up to €60,000 and denial of registry filings affecting the company's legal standing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory if the company satisfies at least two of the following three tests in two consecutive years: total assets exceed €2,850,000; net annual turnover exceeds €5,700,000; average employees exceed 50. Also mandatory where the company is part of a consolidation group under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual accounts under Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable); consolidated accounts under IFRS as endorsed by the EU where applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must keep its ultimate beneficial ownership record accurate on the registral sheet. Any shareholding transfer or UBO change must be reported to the Mercantile Registry within 30 days, accompanied by supporting transfer documentation; the annual accounts deposit process includes verification that the recorded UBO data is currently accurate. Failure to confirm or correct UBO data restricts subsequent corporate registrations.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500 - $1,200 for registered office, registered agent, and maintenance services in Spain
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,700 - $8,700 depending on turnover, asset base, and volume of transactions requiring audit procedures

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate. Newly incorporated entities generally apply a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and eligibility conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Spanish resident SL companies are taxed on worldwide income. Qualifying small enterprises may receive reduced rates under temporary statutory measures. For tax periods beginning in 2025, qualifying micro-enterprises with prior-year turnover below EUR 1 million may apply a reduced progressive rate of 21% on the first EUR 50,000 of taxable profit and 22% on the excess, subject to applicable transitional rules. Newly incorporated entities may qualify for the 15% rate. Tax credits may apply for research and development, technological innovation, audiovisual production, foreign tax, and certain employment or investment activities. The participation exemption may apply to qualifying dividends and capital gains, generally subject to a 5% holding and subsidiary-taxation threshold and a minimum one-year holding period, with the statutory 5% management-expense reduction generally limiting the exemption to 95%. Spain generally permits tax-loss carryforwards without a temporal expiry, but annual utilization is subject to percentage limitations, including the EUR 1 million minimum threshold and larger-company limitations based on prior-year turnover. The schema-prescribed five-year value is therefore not the current Spanish statutory expiry rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where available, or an authorized representative. Modelo 200 is the standard annual return for an SL. Modelo 202 is the periodic Corporate Income Tax instalment-payment form. Modelo 222 applies to entities within a consolidated tax group.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for Modelo 200; three instalment payments annually for Modelo 202 where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200: within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year company closing on 31 December, the normal filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year, subject to electronic-filing and banking-calendar rules. Modelo 202: generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December; the final day is normally extended where the payment is made by direct debit under AEAT rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered address, tax period, activity classification, entity type, accounting period, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL files as a Spanish resident company and must use its Spanish NIF. Non-resident shareholders, directors, lenders, and suppliers do not convert the SL into a non-resident filing vehicle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting balance-sheet data, turnover, operating income, cost of goods sold, depreciation, finance costs, provisions, personnel expenses, and accounting profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Spanish company's statutory accounts under Spanish accounting rules. Transactions with non-resident related parties must reconcile to intercompany agreements, invoices, customs records, and transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary book-to-tax adjustments, non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, impairment adjustments, provisions, finance-cost limitations, tax-exempt income, and prior-year adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish Corporate Income Tax rules rather than the tax treatment of the shareholder or foreign group entity. Foreign taxes are not automatically deductible where a foreign-tax credit or exemption regime applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Available tax losses, losses utilized in the current year, losses carried forward, and percentage limitation calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain documentary evidence for the origin and continuity of losses. Utilization is subject to statutory annual limits and the EUR 1 million minimum utilization threshold; anti-abuse rules may restrict acquired losses following changes in ownership and activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate, gross Corporate Income Tax, tax credits, foreign-tax relief, withholding-tax credits, and final tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply a reduced rate only where the SL satisfies all statutory conditions. Foreign withholding suffered by the SL must be supported by foreign tax certificates and remain within the Spanish credit limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosures, transaction categories, counterparties, amounts, valuation methods, and required supplementary information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include cross-border purchases, sales, financing, guarantees, management fees, royalties, and services involving group companies or other related parties. Amounts must reconcile to the accounting ledger and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish withholding credits, payment account, direct-debit instruction where used, refund request, or outstanding balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding suffered by the SL is creditable only when legally attributable to the SL and supported by the relevant withholding certificate. Shareholder-level withholding is not a credit of the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic submission, authorized-signatory identification, accounting approval, tax-payment evidence, and retention of supporting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent or director should appoint an AEAT-authorized representative where necessary. Corporate records, invoices, customs documents, bank statements, and tax computations should generally be retained for at least the statutory limitation period and longer where loss or credit carryforwards remain open.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with no tax payable generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months. After 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest from the end of the 12-month period. Voluntary filing before an AEAT assessment generally avoids a standard penalty, although interest and surcharges may remain payable. Incorrect or incomplete returns may attract tax penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on concealment, fraud, repeated conduct, and other aggravating factors. Modelo 202 underpayments may generate interest, surcharges, and penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 Corporate Income Tax instalment payment, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters. The instalment is generally calculated using either the prior-year tax-liability method or the current-period accounting-tax-base method, where legally required or elected.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment schedule with three annual instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1 to 20 April, 1 to 20 October, and 1 to 20 December. Large companies and companies using the current-period method may be subject to additional calculation requirements and mandatory electronic payment procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, accounting period, and filing category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's NIF and resident-company status. Do not report the foreign shareholder as the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax-liability basis or current-period tax-base basis, including applicable percentage and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm whether the group-size or turnover rules require the current-period method. The selection must be consistent with the applicable statutory election and prior filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross instalment, applicable reductions or credits, previous instalments, and net amount payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the instalment to management accounts, the prior Modelo 200, expected tax credits, and anticipated tax-loss utilization. Avoid unsupported reductions based solely on foreign group tax forecasts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment account, direct debit, electronic payment reference, authorized representative, and filing confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The account used for payment must be operational for AEAT procedures. Retain the electronic filing receipt and banking confirmation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may trigger the statutory late-payment surcharge, interest, and, where the filing is incorrect or omitted, tax penalties. Failure to make instalments can create a final annual tax shortfall and may be reviewed as a repeated compliance failure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident recipient, subject to exemptions, treaty relief, beneficial-ownership requirements, anti-abuse rules, and domestic exemptions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Spanish payer generally withholds unless a domestic exemption or treaty-reduced rate is properly available. The non-resident recipient should provide a valid certificate of tax residence issued by its competent foreign tax authority, evidence of beneficial ownership, corporate and ownership documentation, and any documents required by the applicable double-tax treaty. The payer should verify treaty entitlement, holding-period and minimum-ownership conditions, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose considerations where applicable, and retain the evidence. Where treaty relief is not applied at source, the recipient may generally seek a refund through the Spanish non-resident tax refund procedure, supported by the residence certificate and withholding evidence. The EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption may apply to dividends paid to a qualifying EU or EEA corporate parent, commonly requiring at least a 5% direct holding or qualifying acquisition value, a minimum one-year holding period, an eligible legal form, subject-to-tax status, and anti-abuse compliance. A foreign parent in a non-EU jurisdiction must normally rely on the relevant treaty or domestic exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Spanish non-resident withholding rate is generally 19% for interest and royalties paid to non-residents, subject to specific statutory rules. Interest and royalty payments to qualifying associated companies in EU Member States may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, commonly requiring a minimum 25% direct or indirect relationship, a minimum one-year holding period, qualifying legal form and tax-subjection conditions, and beneficial ownership. Applicable tax treaties frequently reduce interest and royalty withholding to 0%, 5%, 8%, 10%, or another negotiated rate, depending on the treaty and payment category. Treaty relief requires a valid residence certificate, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse review, and compliance with any treaty procedural requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No single universal Spanish threshold triggers all transfer-pricing documentation. A Spanish Local File is generally required for material related-party transactions, subject to statutory exemptions and simplified documentation. The commonly relevant exemption is that documentation is not required for transactions with the same related person or entity of the same type and under the same valuation method where the aggregate market value does not exceed EUR 250,000 in the relevant tax period, subject to exclusions for specific transactions. A Master File is generally required for Spanish entities belonging to a group with consolidated turnover of at least EUR 45 million, subject to statutory exceptions. Country-by-Country reporting generally applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods may be accepted where the listed methods cannot reliably determine an arm's-length result
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a separate standalone regime titled Economic Substance Regulations comparable to certain offshore jurisdictions. Economic substance is nevertheless relevant through the general anti-abuse rule, the conflict-in-application doctrine, the principal-purpose rule in treaties, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, transfer-pricing requirements, interest limitation, anti-hybrid rules, and EU anti-tax-avoidance legislation. The SL should maintain genuine Spanish management, decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or logistics capability proportionate to its used-heavy-machinery wholesale activity, commercial risk control, inventory and customs records, and banking and accounting substance. A conduit company receiving dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees without commercial functions is exposed to denial of treaty or domestic relief and reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating machinery sales, overstating deductible acquisition or refurbishment costs, fabricating invoices, concealing cash consideration, claiming unsupported losses or credits, or deliberately omitting taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties commonly range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, with interest and collection measures. Tax fraud may become a criminal offence where the evaded tax exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period. Basic tax fraud may carry imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of 1 to 6 times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or organized or particularly sophisticated conduct, may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of 2 to 6 times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil and tax liability where they deliberately participate, negligently fail to prevent the breach, or cause the company to become non-compliant. Criminal conviction can lead to imprisonment, fines, disqualification from public office or management, asset seizure, and restitution. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court in criminal or enforcement proceedings; they are not an automatic consequence of an ordinary tax adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Value Added Tax and customs fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying used excavators or rollers, manipulating customs value or origin, claiming fictitious input VAT, using missing-trader structures, importing without proper customs declarations, or treating domestic sales as exports without proof of transport.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT and customs assessments may include unpaid tax, late-payment interest, confiscation or seizure of goods, and administrative penalties commonly calculated by reference to the unpaid or improperly claimed amount. Serious or organized VAT fraud may also satisfy the criminal tax-fraud threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face joint or subsidiary liability, criminal prosecution for intentional fraud, asset seizure, and disqualification where they direct or knowingly facilitate the conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing machinery from a related foreign company at inflated prices, selling below market value to a group distributor, charging unsupported management fees, using non-arm's-length financing, or failing to document intercompany services and functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make a primary adjustment, impose compensating adjustments where legally available, deny deductions, recharacterize distributions, and impose transfer-pricing documentation penalties. Documentation breaches may attract fixed penalties per omitted or incorrect data point, while underpaid tax may attract percentage-based penalties and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face tax liability and civil claims for deliberate or grossly negligent conduct, especially where the arrangement lacks commercial purpose or causes insolvency. Criminal exposure generally requires intentional conduct meeting the statutory tax-fraud threshold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, treaty abuse, and beneficial-ownership failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, royalties, or sale proceeds through an entity with no personnel, decision-making, commercial risk, or beneficial entitlement to obtain an artificial reduced withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty or domestic withholding relief may be denied, with recovery of withholding tax, interest, surcharges, and penalties. The arrangement may be challenged under Spanish anti-abuse provisions, the principal-purpose rule, beneficial-ownership standards, or the general anti-avoidance doctrine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil and tax liability and, where fraud is intentional and material, criminal liability. Courts may order asset freezing, confiscation, management disqualification, and restitution. A travel ban requires judicial grounds and is not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, using opaque beneficial owners, structuring transactions below reporting thresholds, dealing with sanctioned persons, recycling proceeds through machinery invoices, or failing to identify customers and counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML breaches may result in warnings, public reprimands, license or activity restrictions where applicable, and administrative fines that can reach the statutory maximums applicable to the breach, including material percentage-based or fixed penalties. Money laundering may constitute a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment, fines, and confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be personally liable for intentional participation or serious organizational failures. Criminal money-laundering liability can include imprisonment, fines, disqualification, asset confiscation, and judicial restrictions on movement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Accounting, corporate records, and insolvency misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining false books, failing to record inventory impairment, concealing related-party balances, distributing profits without distributable reserves, continuing to trade while insolvent, or transferring assets to shareholders or group companies before creditor claims are satisfied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include rejection of accounts, tax reassessment, civil damages, restoration of assets, insolvency clawback, director disqualification, and criminal liability for falsification, creditor frustration, or aggravated insolvency misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to cover all or part of the insolvency deficit, return improperly distributed funds, compensate creditors, and bear civil or criminal sanctions. The limited-liability shield does not protect intentional fraud, unlawful distributions, abuse of the company, or personal guarantees.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful dividend distribution and profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends without approved annual accounts, sufficient distributable profit or reserves, satisfying statutory reserve requirements, or withholding and remitting the correct Spanish tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlawful distributions may be recoverable from shareholders who knew or should have known of the defect and from directors who authorized them. Additional Corporate Income Tax, withholding tax, interest, surcharges, and penalties may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for restitution and damages, lose management protection in insolvency, and face criminal exposure where the distribution is part of asset stripping or creditor prejudice.
